prompt: Same model, two ways to store its weights - what actually changes?

options.label: fp16 (16-bit, full precision)
options.content: Largest memory footprint and slowest to move around, but every weight keeps its full precision. Safest choice when a task is sensitive to small errors compounding, or when you have GPU memory to spare.

options.label: int4 (4-bit, quantized)
options.content: Roughly a quarter of the memory footprint and noticeably faster to load and multiply, because there's simply less data to move per weight. Output quality drops slightly - usually not perceptibly for most tasks, since errors from individually-rounded weights average out across millions of them - but the drop is real and grows if you push precision even lower.
